entry.content:
Kriti Yadav, Researcher, RMIT; Data Science Intern, Telecommunications Industry Ombudsman

https://www.linkedin.com/in/kriti-yadav-data-science/

Kriti will show how unstructured customer complaints can be turned into reliable, actionable insights using semantic-scoring and classification pipelines built with Python, sentence transformers, DistilBERT, Azure Machine Learning, Microsoft Fabric, Power BI and LLM-based weak supervision. She'll also cover the human-in-the-loop governance framework, the limitations she hit, and practical recommendations for building trustworthy AI classification systems.

(Talk #2, 32:20)

entry.title: Crossing the Streams: Sand-boxing python applications
entry.summary:
Ben Taylor, Product Engineering Team Lead, Stile Education

https://www.linkedin.com/in/taybenlor/

Ben, a software engineer passionate about EdTech, will share his experience of adapting the Runno sandbox, originally written in TypeScript for browser environments, into a Python package. Over the holidays, Ben released this tool to PyPI …
entry.content:
Ben Taylor, Product Engineering Team Lead, Stile Education

https://www.linkedin.com/in/taybenlor/

Ben, a software engineer passionate about EdTech, will share his experience of adapting the Runno sandbox, originally written in TypeScript for browser environments, into a Python package. Over the holidays, Ben released this tool to PyPI, enabling developers to safely run untrusted code from various languages directly within Python. This talk will cover the challenges of bridging languages, the importance of sandboxing and AI workflows, and how this tool can enhance projects involving LLMs and interactive learning environments.

entry.title: Migrating COBOL data to PostgreSQL using Python and Django
entry.content:
Alan Perkins, Founder, Profound Information

https://www.linkedin.com/in/alanperkins/

This talk will cover the approach and challenges faced in migrating data from a 42 year old COBOL system. The resulting python application processed between 150 million and a billion records every day for over four years.
